terms.gloss: the subject of a sentence or proposition
evidence: Mart. Cap. 4.361; App. Dogm. Plat. 3 (Lewis & Short s.v. subicio)
terms.comment: In the later philosophers “that which is spoken of”, the subject of a proposition; in modern grammars the subject of the verb: est subjectum «vēnit» verbī, it is the subject of the verb “vēnit” (Traupman 242).

phrases.english: It is the subject of the verb “vēnit”.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 242, 248.
